question:
Aviation – Flight Paths Intersection

Flight $P$ moves from $A(1,7,2)$ to $B(5,11,6)$. Flight $Q$ moves from $C(8,2,5)$ to $D(4,6,1)$.

(1) Write vector equations.

(2) Find direction ratios.

(3) Find angle between paths.

(4) Check if perpendicular.

(5) State condition for parallel.

(6) Determine if skew.
explanation:
(1) $\vec r_1=(1,7,2)+\lambda(4,4,4)$ and $\vec r_2=(8,2,5)+\mu(-4,4,-4)$.

(2) Direction ratios $(4,4,4)$ and $(-4,4,-4)$.

(3) $\cos\theta=1/3$ so $\theta=\cos^{-1}(1/3)$.

(4) Not perpendicular since dot product not zero.

(5) Parallel if ratios proportional.

(6) Since not parallel and no common solution, lines are skew.

options.A:
(1) $\vec r_1=(1,7,2)+\lambda(4,4,4)$ and $\vec r_2=(8,2,5)+\mu(-4,4,-4)$
(2) Direction ratios are $(4,4,4)$ and $(-4,4,-4)$
(3) $\theta=90^\circ$
(4) They are perpendicular
(5) Parallel if dot product is zero
(6) They are intersecting lines
options.B:
(1) $\vec r_1=(1,7,2)+\lambda(4,4,4)$ and $\vec r_2=(8,2,5)+\mu(-4,4,-4)$
(2) Direction ratios are $(4,4,4)$ and $(-4,4,-4)$
(3) $\cos\theta=\frac{1}{3}$, so $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)$
(4) They are not perpendicular since dot product is not zero
(5) Lines are parallel if their direction ratios are proportional
(6) They are skew lines since they are not parallel and have no common solution
options.C:
(1) $\vec r_1=(1,7,2)+\lambda(5,11,6)$ and $\vec r_2=(8,2,5)+\mu(4,6,1)$
(2) Direction ratios are $(5,11,6)$ and $(4,6,1)$
(3) $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)$
(4) They are perpendicular
(5) Parallel if endpoints are proportional
(6) They are parallel distinct lines
options.D:
(1) $\vec r_1=(5,11,6)+\lambda(4,4,4)$ and $\vec r_2=(4,6,1)+\mu(-4,4,-4)$
(2) Direction ratios are $(4,4,4)$ and $(-4,4,-4)$
(3) $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)$ only
(4) They are perpendicular
(5) Parallel if coordinates are equal
(6) They intersect at $(1,7,2)$
